title: Article 72 — Power of President to grant pardons, etc., and to suspend, remit or commute sentences in certain cases

content.overview: Article 72 confers on the President the power to grant pardons, reprieves, respites or remissions of punishment, or to suspend, remit or commute the sentence of any person convicted of any offence — (a) in all cases where the punishment or sentence is by a Court Martial; (b) in all cases where the punishment or sentence is for an offence against a law relating to a matter to which the executive power of the Union extends; (c) in all cases where the sentence is a sentence of death. The power does not affect the power of the Governor under Article 161 (or any officer of the Armed Forces under law to suspend, remit or commute a Court Martial sentence).
content.glance: President may pardon/reprieve/respite/remit/suspend/commute: Court Martial; Union-law offences; death sentences. Concurrent with Governor’s Art 161 power for overlapping areas.
content.study:
Article 72(1) power covers:
(a) Court Martial punishments/sentences;
(b) offences against laws on matters within Union executive power;
(c) death sentences.

Clause (2)–(3): does not affect Armed Forces officers’ powers under law regarding Court Martial sentences, or the Governor’s power under Article 161.

Exercise is on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers (Art 74). Judicial review of the process (not substitution of merits) has been recognised in case law at a high level.

Examination: three categories; overlap with Art 161; aid and advice; distinguish pardon types (pardon, reprieve, respite, remission, suspension, commutation).

sections.heading: Scope
sections.body:
1. Court Martial cases.
2. Offences against laws relating to matters within Union executive power.
3. Death sentences.
4. Does not oust Governor’s Art 161 power or Armed Forces officers’ Court Martial powers under law.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What is the President’s pardon power under Article 72?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 72, the President has power to grant pardons, reprieves, respites or remissions of punishment, or to suspend, remit or commute sentences, in cases of Court Martial sentences, offences against laws relating to matters within the Union’s executive power, and death sentences. This does not affect the Governor’s power under Article 161 or powers of Armed Forces officers under law in respect of Court Martial sentences.

examTips: Three categories; concurrent with Art 161; on aid and advice.

keyTakeaways: Art 72: Presidential pardon/commutation power — Court Martial, Union offences, death sentences.
